title: Friday the 13th
build: G64 disk image: a one-line loader, a title program that loads at $2900, a 29,299-byte main program at $5800, two data files at $0C00 and $E000, and a 880-byte program at $0400. One sector on the disk has a bad checksum

records.c: the processor port: set to $36 (BASIC out); show_text_screen clears bit 2 to read the character ROM and sets it again
zero-page byte play_scream uses for the end of the sample, low byte
the end of the sample, high byte
the KERNAL's current key, $40 when none is held; wait_key reads it
a pointer: the source of copy_pages and the text print_string prints
the pointer's high byte
the scream sample's length, low byte, read by play_scream from the sample's first two bytes
the scream sample's length, high byte
the KERNAL's screen page: set to $7C so that CHROUT prints on the screen at $7C00
where TITLE2, the loader of the game's files, loads; the intro jumps there once it is loaded (the loader was not read)

the introduction, entered from the loader when the file TITLE has loaded: black border and background, BASIC banked out, the screen cleared; moves the portraits picture out of the video bank to $8800 (40 pages from $5F40), shows the title picture with the scream, then the licence and the story as text, waiting for a key after each, then the portraits, and loads TITLE2 and jumps to it at $0900
shows the title picture: copies its screen colours ($2DDC) to $7C00 and its colour RAM ($31DC) to $D800, then sets up the picture (show_bitmap)
selects video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA 2, the screen at $7C00 and the bitmap at $4000 ($D018), multicolour on, bitmap mode on

shows the five counsellors' portraits: copies the picture back from $8800 into the bitmap at $4000 (32 pages), its screen colours from $A740 to $7C00 and its colour RAM from $AB40 to $D800, sets the background to dark grey (11) and turns the bitmap on (show_bitmap)
copies X pages from the address in $FB-$FC to the page in A, 256 bytes at a time; the copy's destination is the STA's own operand
the STA whose high byte copy_pages writes with the destination page
the high byte of copy_dest's operand: the destination page, written by copy_pages and counted up a page at a time

with the I/O banked out, copies the character ROM (16 pages from $D000) to $6000, tells the KERNAL the screen is at $7C00 ($0288), points the video chip at the font, clears the screen, turns bitmap and multicolour off, and prints the licence text ($2A35)
prints the story text at $2B68
prints the text at Y (low) and X (high) through CHROUT until a zero byte
the licence screen: "FRIDAY THE 13TH" is a trademark of Paramount Pictures Corporation, manufactured by Domark Ltd under exclusive licence, in PETSCII with colour codes, ended by a zero
the story screen: you and nine friends at Crystal Lake holiday camp, Jason Voorhees's grotto, the bloodstained mask, JASON IS WAITING...., and BEFORE HE DISPOSES OF YOU!, ended by a zero
waits for no key ($C5 = $40), then for a key, so that a key held from before does not count
sets the cursor home in red, opens the file TITLE2 on device 8 with SETLFS and SETNAM, and loads it to the address it was saved from with LOAD
length of the file name, 6
address of the file name, $2DD6

the file name TITLE2

the title picture's third colour of each cell, 1000 bytes and 24 spare, copied to colour RAM at $D800
36 bytes in the file that nothing reads: alternating $00 and $FF, the pattern of the memory the file was saved from

plays the scream over the title picture: a 1-bit sample from $36A0, whose first two bytes give its length ($08FE bytes); each 1 bit turns the volume up with voice 1 on (scream_click), each 0 bit turns it off
volume 15 and a triangle on voice 1 at frequency $F313
volume 0

the scream's last 256 bytes, to $3F9F
